description:
## Goal

Extend `notify_observers/1` in `Filament.Observable.GenServer` so it:
1. Applies each subscriber's `project` function to the new state
2. Compares the result to `subscriber.last_projected`
3. Only sends `{:filament_observable_update, ...}` if the projected value changed
4. Updates `subscriber.last_projected` in the process dictionary when it sends

This prevents components from re-rendering when only irrelevant parts of observable
state changed.

Prerequisite: D2 merged.

## Deviation policy

Any deviation from this spec requires prior approval. Stop work, run
`bw comment <ticket-id> "..."` describing the conflict, reopen the ticket, and await guidance.
Do not improvise.

---

## 1. Update Filament.Observable.GenServer — notify_observers/1

FILE: lib/filament/observable/gen_server.ex

Replace the current `notify_observers/1` body (which always sends) with:

```elixir
def notify_observers(new_state) do
  subs = Process.get(:__filament_subscribers__, %{})

  new_subs =
    Map.new(subs, fn {pid, subscriber} ->
      new_projected = subscriber.project.(new_state)

      if new_projected !== subscriber.last_projected do
        send(
          subscriber.pid,
          {:filament_observable_update, subscriber.fiber_id, subscriber.slot_index, new_projected}
        )
        {pid, %{subscriber | last_projected: new_projected}}
      else
        {pid, subscriber}
      end
    end)

  Process.put(:__filament_subscribers__, new_subs)
  :ok
end
```

Use `!==` (strict structural inequality), NOT `!=` (loose). This is critical: `!==` never
raises on any term (including NaN, functions, pids), whereas `!=` can produce surprising
results for uncomparable types. The behaviour is: if `new_projected !== subscriber.last_projected`
then notify, else skip.

---

## 2. Initialise last_projected on subscribe

The first notification must always fire. Ensure `last_projected: :unset` is set when the
subscriber is stored in `handle_call({:filament_subscribe, ...})`. This is already specified
in D1's Subscriber struct (default `:unset`). Confirm the struct field is initialised to
`:unset` and that `:unset !== any_term` is always true (it is — `:unset` is a unique atom
not produced by projection functions).

---

## 3. Tests

FILE: test/filament/observable/gen_server_test.exs
(add to existing test file from D2)

```elixir
defmodule ProjectionCounter do
  use Filament.Observable.GenServer

  def start_link(n), do: GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, n)
  def init(n), do: {:ok, n}
  def set(pid, n), do: GenServer.call(pid, {:set, n})
  def handle_call({:set, n}, _from, _state) do
    notify_observers(n)
    {:reply, :ok, n}
  end
end
```

Test cases:
1. **first notification always fires** — subscribe with `project: fn n -> n > 5 end`, set to 3 (project = false), assert `{:filament_observable_update, ..., false}` received (even though initial `last_projected` was `:unset`, the projected value false !== :unset)
2. **change triggers notification** — subscribe, set to 3 (project = false), set to 10 (project = true), assert TWO updates received: false then true
3. **no-change skips notification** — subscribe, set to 1 (project = false), set to 2 (project = false), assert only ONE update received (the first one)
4. **nil projection survives** — `project: fn _ -> nil end`, set twice, assert only ONE update (nil !== :unset on first, nil === nil on second)
5. **multiple subscribers with different projections** — sub A: `project: fn n -> n end`, sub B: `project: fn n -> n > 5 end`, set to 3: A gets update (3 !== :unset), B gets false. Set to 4: A gets 4, B gets nothing (false === false).

Run: `mix test test/filament/observable/gen_server_test.exs`

---

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] D2 test suite still passes (no regressions)
- [ ] All 5 new projection test cases pass
- [ ] Dialyzer clean
- [ ] `last_projected` is updated in the process dictionary only when a notification is sent
title: D3: Projection support — per-subscriber project fn, change-or-bust skip
